hooks.how: Hooks in settings.json (project `.gemini/settings.json`, user `~/.gemini/settings.json`, system `/etc/gemini-cli/settings.json`) as {"hooks": {"AfterAgent": [{"type": "command", "command": "...", "name": "...", "timeout": 60000}]}}. `AfterAgent` fires when the agent loop ends, once per turn after the final response. Input: `prompt`, `prompt_response` (the final text), `stop_hook_active` (true inside a retry sequence). Output: `decision: "deny"` (`block` accepted as an alias) rejects the response and triggers a retry turn with `reason` sent to the agent as a new prompt; exit code 2 does the same with stderr as feedback; `continue: false` stops; `systemMessage` shows to the user. Only the JSON object may be printed. Whether hooks run in `-p` mode is not verified. Sources: docs/hooks/index.md and docs/hooks/reference.md in google-gemini/gemini-cli on main, read 2026-09-22.

projection.how: `AfterAgent` carries the final text as `prompt_response` and takes `decision: "block"` (an alias of `deny`) with `reason`, which becomes the next prompt; the hook prints only the JSON object. Merged into the project's settings under `hooks`, the rest of the file left as it was.

headless.how: `goose run -t "<prompt>" --no-session -q` runs one prompt headless: `-t, --text` is the input text, `--no-session` runs without creating or storing a session file, `-q, --quiet` suppresses non-response output and prints only the model response to stdout (`--output-format` defaults to text), so the last line of stdout is the tail of the response. Approvals are the `GOOSE_MODE` environment variable, not a flag: auto, approve, chat, smart_approve, default auto (autonomous: files and tools without approval), so no permission flag is needed and the runner sets nothing. `-r/--resume` is not passed.

headless.how: `grok -p "<prompt>"` (`-p, --single <PROMPT>`) is headless mode: Grok processes the prompt, runs any tools, prints the result to stdout and exits when the response is complete. The default `--output-format plain` is text (json and streaming forms exist; update messages go to stderr), so the last line of stdout is the tail of the final answer. `--permission-mode <MODE>` takes acceptEdits (file edits without a prompt), auto, dontAsk (pre-approved tools only) and bypassPermissions; `--always-approve` (alias `--yolo`, the same as bypassPermissions) runs tool calls without interactive prompts, with deny rules, hooks and admin locks still applied, and is what the docs recommend for scripts. `-r/--resume`, `-c/--continue` and `--fork-session` are not passed.

hooks.how: Hooks are read from `~/.grok/config.toml` (plus managed config) and, for compatibility, from `~/.claude/settings.json`, `<project>/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.cursor/hooks.json` and `<project>/.cursor/hooks.json` (Cursor's camelCase `stop` maps to `Stop`). `Stop` fires when an agent turn ends on a genuine completion and can block the stop (Claude Code-compatible); input has `stopHookActive`, `lastAssistantMessage` (the final text, clipped at 32,768 chars) and `reason` (`end_turn`). Output {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} feeds the reason back as a user message and the agent runs another round; {"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."} forces a stop; exit code 2 blocks with stderr as feedback. After 8 continuations in one turn the gate is overridden; Stop times out at 600 s and fails open. Whether Stop fires in `-p` mode is not stated. Source: docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md in xai-org/grok-build on main, read 2026-09-22.
hooks.why: reads `<project>/.claude/settings.json` and `<project>/.cursor/hooks.json`, both of which the factory writes, so nothing of its own is needed

headless.how: `hermes -z <prompt>` is the documented scripted one-shot entry point: one prompt in, only the agent's final reply as plain text on stdout (no banner, spinner or tool previews), then exit, so the last line of stdout is the tail of the final answer. Exit codes: 0 completed, 2 failed, partial or iteration budget spent, 1 completed with no text, 130 interrupted. Unattended approvals follow `approvals.mode` in ~/.hermes/config.yaml (default `smart`: an auxiliary model auto-approves low-risk flagged commands, denies risky ones and escalates uncertain ones); `--yolo` bypasses the dangerous-command prompts, with `approvals.deny` globs still enforced. `-c/--continue` and `-r/--resume` are not passed.

hooks.how: Shell hooks in the `hooks:` block of ~/.hermes/config.yaml: each is a script given a JSON payload on stdin that answers JSON on stdout, consented to on first use. `post_llm_call` and `on_session_end` are observers whose return is ignored; the one directive that keeps a turn going is `pre_verify`, at the bounded edited-code verify gate, which accepts {"action": "continue", "message": "..."} or {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} — continuation at that gate only, not an every-turn stop hook.
